rows.what the ink shows: An initial open C and several small lower loops remain below the cancellation rule. The heavy rule crosses the middle and terminal letters, preventing a secure expansion to Corollaire.
After A, the low membership curve and bar remain visible between cancellation strokes. The following tall b stem has a small right-hand bowl and a separate low underline.
The inserted C has a small closed oval at its lower right, followed by parentheses enclosing the angular capital A. The zero lies below the main letter height.

The first loop and the following separated c/a strokes, low connecting line and final tall l support le calcul. The last joined group has one upper loop and a long low tail, without enough separated strokes to confirm every letter of de son.
After E, the word starts with a descender, rises through a short r shoulder and has an isolated i dot. A low terminal sweep completes the s before dans.

E and the terminal angular A are clear. Between them are low connected humps, a dot, a taller final hump and a separate open c-shaped stroke; these do not securely distinguish the abbreviation comm. from a longer commute à group.
One vertical shaft descends from the horizontal line to a dark downward arrowhead. The curved incoming arrow at upper left is separate, leaving no second downward shaft to support Downarrow.

The initial d has a closed low bowl and upright stem; the following raised loop and descending angular stroke run into a thick baseline. A detached slant is present above the ending, but the apostrophe and o/u division remain inseparable.

A looped initial leads into two short upright teeth and a rounded crossing group; the following short stroke has a dot and a separate slant above it. The ending is drawn as two flattened strokes before the separate membre.

The opening short stroke is followed by a deep q descender; two detached dots occur in the positions of the two i letters. Between them the long connecting stroke rises to a crossed t, followed by two low humps at the end.
Two very low horizontal groups end in a small raised terminal hook before the separate de. Their interior strokes do not distinguish the n/i/e sequence sufficiently to resolve munie.

Three flattened connected groups follow an initial cup, with a small central tooth and one detached dot above the last group. No separate f stem or r/m division can be distinguished in these reduced strokes.
After clockwise rotation, the left subscript starts with two separate parallel strokes for the opening bar and 1. A crossed plus and slanting A follow, with a long closing bar beyond them.
The right subscript begins with a single 1 stroke followed by a crossed plus. The bar is adjacent to the A after that plus, and a separate long closing bar stands at the far right.
